title: Naturality and shifts of the tensor mate of an arbitrary arrow
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories, with bifunctors $\otimes_{\mathcal C}:\mathcal C\times\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ and $\otimes_{\mathcal D}:\mathcal D\times\mathcal D\to\mathcal D$, both denoted $\otimes$. Let $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ have a specified adjunction $L\dashv R$ with natural unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to RL$ and counit $\varepsilon:LR\to\mathrm{id}$ satisfying the triangle identities [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Fix a natural isomorphism $\mu_{M,P}:L(M\otimes P)\xrightarrow{\sim}LM\otimes LP$. For each $K\in\mathcal C$, $E\in\mathcal D$, and morphism $c:LK\to E$, put
$$F_K(P)=K\otimes P,\quad H_E(P)=E\otimes LP,\quad G_E=RH_E,\quad \beta^c_P=(c\otimes1_{LP})\mu_{K,P},\quad \alpha^c_P=R(\beta^c_P)\eta_{K\otimes P}.$$
Suppose the categories have coherent shifts $[n]$ for $n\in\mathbf Z$, each an auto-equivalence, and $L,R$ and every functor $T_M=M\otimes-$ have coherent natural shift comparisons, as in [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker]. Write $l,r,t^M$ for these comparisons. Require the tensor comparisons to be natural in the fixed input $M$, require $\eta$ to commute with every shift for the induced comparison of $RL$, and require $\mu_{K,-}:LF_K\to T_{LK}L$ to commute with the composite comparisons for every $K,n$. In detail put
$$a_{n,P}=l_{n,F_KP}L(t^K_{n,P}),\quad b_{n,P}=t^{LK}_{n,LP}T_{LK}(l_{n,P}),\quad h_{n,P}=t^E_{n,LP}T_E(l_{n,P}),\quad g_{n,P}=r_{n,H_EP}R(h_{n,P}),$$
and assume $b_{n,P}\mu_{K,P[n]}=\mu_{K,P}[n]a_{n,P}$ and $r_{n,LX}R(l_{n,X})\eta_{X[n]}=\eta_X[n]$.
Then for all $K,E,c,P,n$,
$$h_{n,P}\beta^c_{P[n]}=\beta^c_P[n]a_{n,P},\qquad g_{n,P}\alpha^c_{P[n]}=\alpha^c_P[n]t^K_{n,P}.$$
Moreover, for $K'\in\mathcal C$, $E'\in\mathcal D$, $c':LK'\to E'$, $a:K\to K'$, $b:E\to E'$ with $bc=c'L(a)$, and every $p:P\to P'$, one has
$$(b\otimes Lp)\beta^c_P=\beta^{c'}_{P'}L(a\otimes p),\qquad R(b\otimes Lp)\alpha^c_P=\alpha^{c'}_{P'}(a\otimes p).$$
No exactness, tensor associator, unit object, or invertibility of $c$ or $\alpha^c$ is required.
